chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Ayyūb ibn al-Ḥurr, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding the saying:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And whoever is given wisdom, then indeed he has been given abundant good.”
So he عليه السلام said: “Obedience to Allah and recognition of the Imam.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam; the divinely designated guide whose recognition is part of wisdom
key_terms.الْحِكْمَةَ: wisdom; interpreted here as divinely guided understanding expressed through obedience and right recognition
key_terms.خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا: abundant good; the immense benefit granted through true wisdom
key_terms.طَاعَةُ: obedience; compliance with the command of Allah

ai.seo_question: What does “wisdom” mean in Qur'an 2:269 according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration explains the Quranic mention of wisdom as obedience to Allah and recognition of the Imam. It presents true wisdom as not merely intellectual insight, but as rightly guided obedience joined with knowledge of divinely appointed religious authority.
